name: Seoul Streetscapes: Pleasant, Neutral or Unpleasant for Walking
description:
Method replication: participants see 25 street views from the Seoul metropolitan area and answer "What do you think the urban environment in the image is like overall for walking?" with Unpleasant (1), Neutral (2) or Pleasant (3). The images are not the paper's stimuli (62 Google Street View views fetched for this template inside the paper's Seoul bounding box, field of view 90°, facing the direction of travel, 2018–2025 captures).

Original study: Lee, Choi & Hwang (2025), "Automatic method to predict visual pleasantness and unpleasantness of streetscapes and identify key microscale components for improving pedestrian environments", Developments in the Built Environment 22, 100652. 10,000 online respondents (5,000 panel members and 5,000 recruited through online advertisements) each rated one set of 25 images on the three-category scale, giving 50 ratings for each of 5,000 images (Seoul Google Street View, AI Hub walkway photos, Cityscapes, Kakao Road View and the authors' own photos); a model then predicted pleasantness and SHAP identified the microscale components behind it.

Differences from the original study: (1) Seoul Google Street View images only, not the mixed image sources; (2) participants draw 25 images at random from 62 instead of fixed survey sets; (3) the component detection and prediction model are not part of the template.
author: Lee, Choi & Hwang
